slides.heading: Min Heap Construction
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Medium · Heaps
slides.narration: Let's solve Min Heap Construction, a medium heaps problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: Array-backed min-heap with buildHeap (O(n) sift-down), siftUp, siftDown, peek, insert and remove.
slides.narration: Here's the problem. Array-backed min-heap with buildHeap (O of n sift-down), siftUp, siftDown, peek, insert and remove.

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: A heap is an array tree; sift up after insert, sift down after removal.
slides.narration: A heap is an array tree; sift up after insert, sift down after removal.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: Insert one by one with siftUp → O(n log n)
Bottom-up siftDown from the last parent → O(n)
Most nodes are near the bottom and barely move
slides.narration: Inserting elements one at a time costs n log n. Building bottom-up, sifting down from the last parent to the root, is linear, because most nodes sit near the bottom and move only a little.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 1. Build by sifting down from the last parent
2. Insert at the end and sift up
3. Remove by swapping root with last and sifting down
slides.narration: Step by step. First, build by sifting down from the last parent. Second, insert at the end and sift up. Third, remove by swapping root with last and sifting down.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Start: arbitrary array as a tree
slides.narration: View the array as a complete binary tree: children of index i are at two i plus one and two i plus two.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: siftDown index 3 (value 17)
slides.narration: Sift down the value 17 at index 3, swapping with its smaller child until it's no bigger than both children.

slides.heading: Java solution (1/2)
slides.narration: Build heap sifts down from the last parent to index zero. Sift down picks the smaller child, stops if it isn't smaller, otherwise swaps and continues. Sift up swaps with the parent while the parent is bigger.

slides.heading: Java solution (2/2)
slides.narration: Build heap sifts down from the last parent to index zero. Sift down picks the smaller child, stops if it isn't smaller, otherwise swaps and continues. Sift up swaps with the parent while the parent is bigger.

slides.heading: Complexity
bullets: Time: build O(n), insert/remove O(log n), peek O(1)
slides.narration: Time is build O of n, insert or remove O of log n, peek constant. Space is O of n.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
bullets: Remove: swap root with last, pop, siftDown
slides.narration: The last parent is at n minus two over two. Always swap with the smaller child. Remove swaps the root with the last element, pops, and sifts down.

slides.heading: Interview tips & follow-ups
bullets: Follow-up: k-th largest, merge k sorted lists
slides.narration: Be ready to explain the linear build. Heaps power k-th largest and merging k sorted lists.

slides.heading: Recap
bullets: A heap is an array tree; sift up after insert, sift down after removal.
Complexity: build O(n), insert/remove O(log n), peek O(1)
slides.narration: To recap Min Heap Construction: A heap is an array tree; sift up after insert, sift down after removal. Try re-implementing it from scratch without looking.
